title: Barmaid work in New Orleans after her return
summary: Back in New Orleans around 1938 she tended bar on Rampart Street and sang along to the music box. She stayed because of her mother's illness.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: You said it was about 1938 when your mother got married? 38 yeah

And you didn't sing after you came back to New Orleans? No I told you how I tried to get in and I couldn't get in so then I just What sort of job did you hold on here? Were you working then or were you just Yeah I went and a friend of mine had a bar room on Rampart Street it was during the holidays he said he wanted some extra help he asked me did I think I could do it I said well what is to do? I said serve some beer and some mixed drinks I said I did that at my house serve company you know high balls I think that's all you got to do I said okay well yeah I'll do it and so I went to help him out and I liked it and the people liked me and I stayed there and I worked in his place I guess I must have been there on and off about three years or more you know at Green's place on Rampart Street I was the bar made there and on Sundays they used to come tell me all their trouble he's called me the voice of experience Did you do anything while you were at the bar? Well yes when they put on a piece you know on the music box my favorite piece was Bing Crosby's brother Bob Crosby's the music box was a little bit of a song and I was like oh I'm sorry now and when they play that I'd just bellow out and they'd always say oh Miss Lizzy you ought to go and make records you ought to go and show Miss Lizzy oh you can sing good they didn't know that I had been a singer you know then that piece when that piece came out about oh it was something like this I'm dancing with tears in my eyes and I used to sing that you know well so many pieces they put on the music box well when they put them on I'd sing you see well a lot of the people who knew me and knew of me singing a long time and they used to tell me well Liz you ain't lost nothing you still can go kid you know they'd say those things to me you know then I when I left that job the man who owns the Kitten Club on Ramport Street Johnny Robita he hired me to come and work in his take care of his liquor store for him well I used to do the same thing there you know whenever they'd put pieces on there and one night there was some customers there and said I tell you what Johnny after you close up let's have a cabaret so just this man's party and another party it must have been altogether about 15 and Johnny and myself and we had a cabaret I entertained him with the music box singing with the records on the music record I must have made about $25 them giving me tips you know
so all along even though you weren't actually singing the cabaret you did keep on singing on your own
